rows.acceptance: Pin C# Studio backend, Studio JS/CSS and Rust engine/desktop commit SHAs in a machine-readable baseline; all parity claims name those SHAs.
rows.scope_note: Machine-readable baseline: code HEAD, reference commit, catalog hash, 13 source hashes, toolchain.

rows.acceptance: Every visible web feature, route-derived behavior and desktop-only behavior has owner, source path, status, test and waiver; omissions fail the audit.
rows.scope_note: 49 feature rows; 229/229 requirement IDs owned after the explicit gate-owned resolution in section 5.

rows.requirement: Distinguish behavioral parity from implementation parity
rows.acceptance: REST and browser storage are replaced by in-process native mechanisms; parity tests compare behavior, not transport or widget technology.
rows.scope_note: Transport-to-native mapping plus the consequences for parity tests.

rows.acceptance: Desktop commands use the same Rust kernel as Rust runner; no math/parser/precision semantics are reimplemented in widgets or renderer.
rows.scope_note: RealEngine owns lovelace_lang::Engine and delegates eval/format; no math semantics in the desktop.

rows.acceptance: Release remains blocked when any P0 acceptance test is absent, skipped, stale, unrun or failed, regardless of headless suite count.
rows.scope_note: Gate exits non-zero on unevidenced rows.

rows.acceptance: Every non-parity choice has human-approved rationale, expiry/review criterion and evidence; absence is not counted as equivalence.
rows.scope_note: Seven deviations with owner, status, rationale, review criterion and evidence.

rows.acceptance: Record deterministic reference state/output/diagnostics/plots for the named web Studio journeys and execute corresponding desktop scenarios.

rows.requirement: Separate visual, functional and performance acceptance
rows.acceptance: Release scorecard reports three independent gates and never substitutes screenshots for semantics or engine unit tests for real-window behavior.
Publish Windows, Linux and macOS target matrix, clearly marking initial release and later ports; no platform claim without a built, run GUI test.
rows.scope_note: Published matrix: Windows 11 x64 initial release; Win10 and Linux/macOS not claimed.

rows.acceptance: Delivery plan prioritizes editor responsiveness, real cancellation, readability, working plots and useful inspection before optional decoration.

rows.requirement: Choose and validate a native rendering stack
rows.acceptance: Run a time-boxed spike comparing candidate Rust UI frameworks against real editor, accessibility, text/IME, plotting and docking acceptance scenarios; record choice.
rows.scope_note: Windows spike + iced/slint probes measured; Linux half deferred by DEC-006; IME composition not driven.

rows.acceptance: Production desktop has no embedded webview, JavaScript engine or mandatory localhost service; application operates with all network interfaces disabled.
rows.scope_note: Production binary links only user32/gdi32/comctl32/comdlg32/kernel32; selftest no-network-imports inspects the PE import table.

rows.acceptance: Headless app state and commands are independent of platform window handles; native renderer consumes state and publishes typed commands.
Worker emits RunStarted/StepStarted/StepComputed/StepReused/SubProgress/Output/Plot/Diagnostic/Completed/Cancelled with run and document IDs.

rows.requirement: Never execute evaluation on the UI thread
rows.acceptance: Even a 30-second script leaves pointer, keyboard, window close, pane resize and animations responsive; automated GUI watchdog verifies.
Only one computation mutates a document engine at a time; concurrent requests are rejected or queued with clear UI policy.

rows.requirement: Permit independent documents to run concurrently
rows.acceptance: With tab A busy, tab B can run and cancel and tab A continues unaffected; no process-wide engine lock.
Every event has document ID, run ID, source revision and sequence; events from obsolete revisions never overwrite current pane state.
Worker passes a cooperative token into evaluator, high-precision math and symbolic loops; cancellation interrupts a test operation rather than only setting UI state.
UI gets typed numeric, array, record, symbolic and diagnostic projections; display text is not reparsed to infer structure.
Platform-specific unsafe code stays in small adapters with reviewed invariants; shared UI, workspace, execution and settings logic is safe Rust.

rows.requirement: Resist unbounded memory and event queues
rows.acceptance: Progress and output delivery has coalescing/backpressure and bounded storage without losing terminal events, final result or required diagnostics.
Product design describes a calm scientific workbench: information-dense, precise, low-noise, professional; final screens are reviewed against reference mockups.

rows.requirement: Ship excellent dark and light themes
rows.acceptance: Both themes have complete token sets for surfaces, text, borders, focus, selection, syntax, plots and semantic status; no unthemed native child control.
Layout spacing uses 4/8/12/16/24/32 logical-pixel tokens with documented exceptions; an automated style lint flags raw one-off margins.
UI uses legible proportional controls and configurable monospaced code/output; titles, labels, table text and metadata have consistent hierarchy.
No gradients, heavy glass effects or gratuitous animations obscure content; active pane, selection, errors and actions remain legible in both themes.
Every button/input/tab/menu/popup/splitter implements rest, hover, pressed, disabled, selected, focus and error states with consistent interaction.

rows.requirement: Provide semantic color without color dependence
rows.acceptance: Success, failure, progress, cancelled and warning use text/icon/shape plus color; color is never the only carrier of state.
First launch and empty variables/functions/plots/logs/inspector panes explain what to do next and offer an appropriate next action.
Normal text reaches WCAG AA 4.5:1 and large text/non-text UI indicators reach 3:1 in each theme, validated from rendered colors.
Run is discoverable in toolbar and menu; Cancel visibly replaces or accompanies Run while active and communicates progress.
One consistent icon family, stroke weight and size; icons with ambiguous meaning include visible text or tooltips with shortcut.
Primary viewport keeps editor and output prominent; secondary metadata, verbose JSON and advanced settings open on demand.
Compact, comfortable and default density modes change row height/padding but preserve layout, accessible hit areas and typography hierarchy.
Success uses subtle confirmation; errors are near their cause; progress never uses indefinite spinner where measured work exists.
Animation is modest (typically 120–200 ms) and reduced-motion setting removes nonessential motion while maintaining feedback.
The 900×600, 1280×800 and 1920×1080 layouts remain usable without clipping, accidental overlays or illegible content.
Title, toolbar, menus and window controls feel native while retaining one cross-platform product identity; no hand-drawn imitation of OS close buttons.
Fresh launch presents working example/Open File/New Script affordances plus a concise keyboard hint; user can run first script in at most two actions.

rows.requirement: Make the editor the primary surface
rows.acceptance: At default 1280×800 editor receives at least ~45% width and clear visual priority without making results/plot inaccessible.
Visible reachable Editor, Workspace, Graph, Logs and Symbolic Inspector; each has a titled pane and its own empty/error states.
Mouse and keyboard resize all adjacent panes with min sizes; double click or command restores sensible defaults.
After close/relaunch the layout matches user choices including hidden/maximized panes, unless screen geometry makes that unsafe.
User can maximize editor or graph without losing document state; one action returns to previous layout.
At least Standard, Explore (larger plot) and Focus (larger editor) presets, with reversible user customization.
Workspace, graph and inspector may be rearranged or detached without losing state; optional feature cannot block core parity.
Status always reports active document, revision, precision, cursor line/column, run state and recent elapsed time without truncating essential fields.
rows.scope_note: Product window status strip: welcome.lv | rev 0 | precision 1000 | Ln 1, Col 1 | run Finished + 14 ms last run.

rows.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd+Tab switches documents; a documented shortcut rotates focus between panes with visible focus.
Graph and Inspector clearly indicate which run/document produced current content; no silent cross-tab displays.
At minimum supported size ancillary panes collapse to tabs or drawer rather than shrink editor below usable width.
Run, Cancel, precision, search, tab close and pane visibility retain consistent placement across layouts.

rows.requirement: Replace multiline Win32 EDIT as the primary code editor
rows.acceptance: Real editor supports rich text decorations, gutter, completions, line diagnostics and virtualization; no plain textarea/EDIT as release fallback.
Numbers, exact rationals, strings/interpolation, keywords, operators, function definitions, builtins, delimiters, brackets and symbolic tokens highlight contextually.
Completion includes keywords, registered builtins, signatures, user functions, live variables and snippets from active engine; values update after execution.
Typing `sqrt(` or `compile(` shows signature and active parameter; documentation is from registered metadata, never duplicate hardcoded text.
Completion/palette search ranks exact prefix first and tolerates useful nonprefix matches without blocking typing.
Errors show underlines and gutter markers at exact reported range with hover tooltip and keyboard navigation, including UTF-16 astral cases.

rows.requirement: Show current line and matching braces
rows.acceptance: Caret line has subtle emphasis; matching `()[]{}` highlighted with clear unmatched indicator.
Indent/outdent selection, smart Enter, auto-close configurable brackets, tab-width and tabs/spaces setting work with the language grammar.
Find, replace, replace-all, case-sensitive, whole-word and optional regex search are reversible and highlight all matches.
Go to line, go to matching bracket, find symbol in file and keyboard document navigation function without pointer input.
At least multiple carets, select next match and column selection; undo remains coherent across all cursors.
Burst typing is coalesced; selection/caret positions restored; all editing actions, replacements and auto-format are undoable per document.

rows.requirement: Preserve file encoding and newline policy
rows.acceptance: Open/save UTF-8, BOM handling and CRLF/LF round-trip without unrequested rewrites; clearly warn on unsupported encoding.
Diagnostic offsets, selections and source ranges correctly convert UTF-16 <-> Rust byte/grapheme positions on emoji, combining marks and newlines.
Always 1-based source line/column (as in web Studio); moving cursor and selecting text updates promptly.
A 500 KB/5,000-line script supports 60 Hz scroll target on reference hardware and typing input p95 under 16 ms; measure in GUI.

rows.requirement: Use IME and international input correctly
rows.acceptance: Compose accented and East-Asian text without losing composition, double committing or invalidating undo; platform UI test required.

rows.requirement: Offer editor zoom and font control
rows.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd plus/minus adjusts editor font size; cursor, selection and diagnostics remain aligned and readable.
Right-click or command palette supports Run selection/line where valid, Copy, Paste, Go to line and Show help.

rows.requirement: Show modified lines and run markers
rows.acceptance: Gutter distinguishes dirty source, computed/reused statement and error using consistent icon/tooltip, never replacing actual diagnosis.
Completions dismiss via Esc, preserve text/selection, and do not hijack typing or cover the active line for long.
Every tab owns buffer, engine, variables, functions, precision, revision, cache, diagnostics and last figure; tests show no leakage.
New/Open/Save/Save As/Close use native dialogs; unmodified file round-trips byte-identically under chosen newline and encoding policy.
Close tab, close window and Quit offer Save/Discard/Cancel; Cancel leaves buffer and focus untouched.

rows.requirement: Support recent files and reopen session
rows.acceptance: Recent files list deduplicates and removes missing paths; relaunch restores tab order/path and active tab.

rows.requirement: Autosave unsaved buffers for crash recovery
rows.acceptance: Edits are journaled atomically to a recovery directory; forced process termination then restart offers intact recovery before overwriting anything.
External edit while tab open offers Reload/Compare/Keep; silent overwrite is forbidden.
Dropping one or more .ls files opens tabs; duplicates focus existing tab unless user requests another independent session.

rows.requirement: Keep editor buffer separate from runtime state
rows.acceptance: Loading or editing a file never automatically executes code; each run explicitly targets a source snapshot.

rows.requirement: Preserve per-document precision and formatting settings
rows.acceptance: Two tabs can have different precision and ASCII/Unicode preferences; selection and process restart do not cause cross-talk.
On restart, restore files/unsaved text/layout; any nonrestored computed variables/functions are explicitly shown as reset until rerun.
Reset Engine is a separately labeled action with clear consequence; clearing variables alone does not reset functions.

rows.requirement: Support tab reorder and close shortcuts
rows.acceptance: Mouse drag reorder and Ctrl/Cmd+W, Ctrl/Cmd+Tab and middle-click behave consistently.
An open file renamed/deleted externally remains editable and warns before save; original data is never silently lost.
Settings and recovery documents carry schema version and are migrated or backed up with warning; corruption never crashes startup.
Ctrl/Cmd+Enter starts a background run and reports running state within 100 ms even when evaluation lasts 30 seconds.
Logs input executes a one-liner in active document engine, appends result, and does not change editor source.
After each committed statement, variables, functions, log output, plots, revision and diagnostics reflect the same coherent engine snapshot.
UI shows completed/total statements, current label and reused count, with stable progress and cancellable status.
Long sqrt/pi/factorial or comparable operations publish human-readable phase and fraction; progress stays meaningful and monotonic where defined.
Cancelling a real long-running script ends work cooperatively, returns UI to idle and never requires terminating the application.
Contract defines which completed statements remain committed and what happens to in-flight statement; tests compare with web Studio contract.
Representative cancellation-aware loops stop within 2 s after request on reference hardware; uninterruptible kernels report why and are budgeted.
Queued, Running, Cancelling, Completed, Cancelled, Failed and Stale states have distinct labels and terminal events.

rows.requirement: Reject duplicate active runs per tab
rows.acceptance: Pressing Run during active run cannot corrupt engine; explicit queue/reject behavior is observable.
Tab A long calculation does not prevent tab B execution or cancellation.

rows.requirement: Protect against stale results after source edits
rows.acceptance: Result event includes snapshot revision; editing while run active never falsely presents stale result as current; user can inspect old result with label.
On error or cancellation, completed-statement workspace and outputs remain consistent; no half-written variable or duplicate print line.
Diagnostics display code, category, message, line, column and suggestions; user can jump to source and retry after correction.
Computed/reused modes, elapsed times and total run time are inspectable without rerunning and without conflating cached timing with work performed.

rows.requirement: Prevent UI starvation from output floods
rows.acceptance: 10,000 emitted log events do not freeze editor; visible log updates batch without changing log order or final integrity.

rows.requirement: Handle engine panics and worker failures gracefully
rows.acceptance: A simulated worker failure produces recoverable error state, releases run lock and preserves buffer/recovery files; process remains usable.

rows.requirement: Make progress feedback informative rather than noisy
rows.acceptance: Progress surfaces a compact inline indicator for short jobs and an expandable detail view for long jobs, without modal interruption.

rows.requirement: Expose precision controls on the execution bar
rows.acceptance: One visibly labeled input sets computation/display precision for the active session; invalid values fail locally with clear guidance.
A `setprecision(n)` statement updates toolbar, engine, cache invalidation and affected value presentation consistently.
Top-level statement slicing, normalized source hashes and per-document computation cache follow reference behavior; no naïve whole-file rerun substitute.

rows.requirement: Track variable and function read dependencies
rows.acceptance: Editing one variable definition recomputes dependent statements transitively, while independent statements report reused status.
Redefining a function invalidates all call sites and dependent calculations, including functions that call that function.
`print`, `plot`, `setprecision` and other effectful calls rerun rather than replaying stale side effects.
Precision-dependent cache keys include compute settings; a precision change cannot reuse an old low-precision result.
Cache dependency hashes derive from full canonical typed value, never truncated display or formatted tooltip.

rows.requirement: Preserve code order and scope semantics
rows.acceptance: Reused assignments reproduce correct downstream visible state without leaking function-local or block-local variables.
Progress and diagnostics report computed/reused count from actual cache hits; instrumentation can falsify the claim.

rows.requirement: Offer an explicit full rerun option
rows.acceptance: Run All Fresh clears only execution memoization for active tab and yields the same values/output as incremental run.
After random edits and cache invalidations, incremental output equals a fresh-run engine snapshot for the identical script and settings.
Cache uses documented memory limits and deterministic eviction; cache eviction never changes results.
Show name, kind and display value for all globals including `_`, sorted by ordinal name by default.

rows.requirement: Provide function table with source distinctions
rows.acceptance: Show name, parameters, builtin/user/plugin origin and summary when available; counts agree with current engine registry.

rows.requirement: Delete one variable without side effects
rows.acceptance: Per-row delete removes only selected variable, updates revision/completions and invalidates affected cache; functions unchanged.
Clear Variables empties globals but retains user-defined functions, matching Studio; regression test fails current rebuild-engine workaround.
Text search filters tables and supports keyboard focus, clear and match navigation; large registries stay responsive.
Numbers, matrices, complex, record and symbolic values render readable previews; detailed content opens without truncating in memory.
Copy display, canonical and JSON/structured data when available; copy preserves exact numerical digits.
Function rows offer signature, help, insert call/example and user-function source navigation where available.
Changing active tab switches workspace and plot to matching engine in same repaint, even during another tab’s run.
Workspace title indicates active tab, revision and whether values are live, cached or from a previous run.
Huge integers and symbolic expressions use selectable scrolling/copy rather than forcing entire value into table cell or trimming source.
Recursive typed renderer uses engine structured values and does not reconstruct arrays or records by parsing pretty strings.
Where supplied, show Natural/Integer/Real/Complex kind, exact/approximate, precision and truncation reasons without suggesting unproven exactness.

rows.requirement: Present arrays and matrices as spatial structures
rows.acceptance: N-dimensional shapes and element kinds are visible; 2-D matrices use readable rows/columns and large arrays virtualize.
Solve, inverse, compile, limit and transform records can be expanded/collapsed by field without data loss.
Symbolic result has visible pretty text and optionally expandable canonical representation, domain, free symbols and node count.
Selecting result detail uses captured value and revision; changing source after run does not silently recompute inspected value.
Numeric values can be copied/exported at full precision even when display is clipped for readability.
Error detail shows code, category, exact message, source location and optional structured signature/hints; no opaque generic failure.
Record/array explorer indicates path (e.g. result.solutions[1].bindings) and allows backtracking without resetting expansion.
Rendering a million-digit result or 100k matrix cells neither blocks UI nor allocates one widget per element.
Dedicated Results view (or pinned inspector) keeps the last typed result while Logs displays chronological events; toggling is one click.
Display pretty, canonical, expression tree, current assumptions, simplification trace and MathIR, where engine supplies them.
Inspector operates on last committed result from active document, not on current unsaved editor text or a background fresh evaluation.
Tree supports expand/collapse, node type, child order, copy node canonical form, and keyboard traversal.
Nonzero/domain/branch conditions are typed symbolic relations, distinguishable from plain text notes.
Trace displays rule identifier, before/after, classification, required conditions and applicability without hiding conditional rewrites.
Partial, Unevaluated and conditional results cannot be presented as fully Solved/Exact; explicit status near the result.
IR view is monospaced, scrollable, selectable with syntax-like instruction highlighting, copy and export.
Selecting a symbolic subtree highlights corresponding pretty/canonical section when mappings are available, otherwise no misleading link.
An expression that cannot lower to MathIR shows a specific reason and leaves other inspector sections usable.
Offer Copy canonical, Insert pretty, Copy MathIR and inspect assumptions with clear action labels; no silent script execution.

rows.requirement: Avoid rendering giant symbolic trees eagerly
rows.acceptance: Tree initially loads bounded depth and virtualizes deeper views; expand remains responsive for >=10k nodes.

rows.requirement: Match full supported Studio plot output
rows.acceptance: Render all SVG elements/attributes actually emitted by Lovelace plotting, including text, polyline, path, clipping and labels; screenshot comparison verifies.
Current minimal polyline/text parser is not accepted as SVG parity; use a complete supported SVG renderer and document supported feature set.
At 100/150/200% scale, strokes, labels and mathematical text remain sharp and correctly positioned with no clipping.
Wheel/buttons zoom around pointer, drag pans, one-click Fit restores full plot and 100% reset is available.
Title and active document/run identity appear with plot; opening other tab never silently shows another tab’s chart.
Save SVG preserves engine bytes; PNG export supports chosen dimensions/scaling and transparent/opaque background options.
Copy Image produces usable bitmap; Copy SVG produces vector data where OS supports it.
Malformed/oversized SVG produces bounded, informative failure without crashes, file access or network loads.

rows.requirement: Persist last plot per active document
rows.acceptance: After successful run plot stays inspectable until replaced/reset and is isolated between tabs.
Plot focus offers keyboard zoom/pan and readable point/cursor values when plot data supports it.

rows.requirement: Provide sensible no-plot and error states
rows.acceptance: Graph pane says No plot yet or Plot unavailable with reason and next action; no blank white mystery pane.
rows.scope_note: Graph pane empty state 'No plot yet. Run a script that calls plot(...).' visible in product-typed.png; post-run UIA shows a rastered plot canvas.

rows.requirement: Keep rendering off UI thread for heavy SVG
rows.acceptance: Complex plot rasterization occurs in worker with cancellation and cached zoomable bitmap/vector scene; GUI remains responsive.

rows.requirement: Allow plot history within a session
rows.acceptance: Optional mini-gallery allows compare/return to previous plots with source and timestamp; feature cannot gate web parity.
Repeated polls/events, reruns and cancellation never duplicate print lines or change order; byte-sensitive tests cover line endings.
Logs distinguish echo, stdout, result, diagnostic, timing and progress with readable icons, text and timestamps optional.
Enter executes active session command and clears input only after accepting request; previous commands are navigable with keyboard.
Click diagnostic opens and focuses source, highlights position, and provides copyable full error details.
Copy selected, copy all, clear current view and save log actions work with keyboard and context menu.
When storage cap is reached show truncated-history indicator and offer export of available full run log if configured; never hide current fatal error.
Display total and per-statement elapsed with units; cached runs identify reused count and avoid implying reused output was recomputed.
Filter by errors, outputs, run and document without changing stored event order.
Success/fail/cancel indication visible without intrusive modal; long-running jobs receive optional desktop notification only by user opt-in.

rows.requirement: Keep performance stable under log load
rows.acceptance: A run with 100k log records remains scrollable via virtualization and bounded live updates; no quadratic text-control replacement.
All commands and pane actions accessible without mouse; an automated keyboard journey completes primary tasks.

rows.requirement: Support screen reader roles and names
rows.acceptance: Windows UIA and corresponding platform accessibility trees expose name/role/value/state for editor, tabs, tables, buttons and progress.
Every focusable control has visible 3:1 focus indicator; focus never becomes invisible in dark or light mode.
125–200% DPI/text scale retains readable buttons/labels and usable layout without clipped content.
Users can configure mono font and 12–24 pt range, line-height and optionally ligatures; all decorations remain aligned.
OS theme change updates controls and plot chrome without losing user focus, run or document state.
Help > Keyboard Shortcuts and command palette display all global and editor shortcuts.

rows.requirement: Avoid conflicts with IME and screen readers
rows.acceptance: Text composition and shortcut accelerators do not steal native IME shortcuts or screen-reader navigation.
High contrast appearance uses semantic tokens rather than merely raising window brightness; contrast validated.
OS reduced-motion preference disables decorative animations while retaining progress values and completion feedback.
Most interactive targets are >=32×32 logical pixels; compact density exceptions preserve alternative keyboard access.
Errors include icon, text and location; color-blind tests identify errors and successes without hue.
Controls and errors use concise, predictable text; abbreviations have tooltips; accessible description includes action and consequence.
ASCII/Unicode setting updates structured result, workspace and logs consistently; missing glyphs fall back without tofu squares.

rows.requirement: Support native file dialogs and clipboard
rows.acceptance: Open/Save/Save As, paste and clipboard integration work via OS APIs with expected keyboard shortcuts.
App launches, evaluates, plots and opens files with network disabled; no HTTP listener or surprise external requests.
Embedded SVG external references and active content do not trigger network/file reads or script execution.
Saving to existing changed file prompts before overwrite; atomic temp-write/rename and recovery preserve original on failure.
Fonts fall back to OS-installed fonts; syntax/theme/icon assets are bundled or resolved offline; no CDN at runtime.
Windows APPDATA, Linux XDG, macOS Application Support are used; no writes to installed binary directory by default.
Signed or notarized where applicable, versioned binaries for supported OS/arch, reliable uninstall and OS integration.
Opening a .ls file from shell launches or focuses desktop with that file, without unexpected execution.

rows.requirement: Expose clear error on unsupported platform
rows.acceptance: A platform without UI support is explicitly marked unsupported by release metadata, not silently shipped as headless placeholder.
Keyboard modifiers, dialogs, caret/IME, clipboard and DPI tested on every advertised platform.
User can export redacted app version/config/logs for bug reports without private source content unless explicitly opted in.
On reference machine cold start to interactive editor p95 <= 2.0 s and warm start <= 1.0 s; measure signed release binary.
Typing/caret movement p95 <= 16 ms and no input freeze >100 ms under normal work, measured with a live GUI profiler.
500 KB/5k-line document maintains >=55 fps p95 scrolling on reference desktop; 10k-line stress run is explicitly reported.
Run button/shortcut acknowledges within 100 ms; worker scheduling not blocked by rendering or queued logs.
Cancel action updates visible state within 100 ms and invokes token immediately; termination meets RUN cancellation bound for cooperative workloads.
Updating 10k variable/function rows takes <=200 ms to visible state via diff/virtualization, without recreating all children.
Typical SVG <100 KB fits pane in <=250 ms after receipt; complex >1 MB remains interactive and shows pending state.
Idle process does not continuously poll at high rate or consume >2% of one reference CPU core; measure with window open.

rows.requirement: Avoid quadratic undo and text copying
rows.acceptance: 10k typed characters do not cause unbounded full-buffer clones per keystroke; memory/CPU profiling confirms acceptable scaling.
Invalid config and recovery files produce warning/default/backup, never launch crash or unrecoverable data loss.

rows.requirement: Monitor resource budgets for enormous math
rows.acceptance: Extreme precision requests receive estimated memory/time warning or budget refusal; no uncontrolled process abort for documented refusal classes.
Renderer crash or invalid plot does not corrupt engine/document; recoverable error surfaces and next run still works.

rows.requirement: Maintain a golden web-to-desktop journey suite
rows.acceptance: Each reference journey has input, action sequence, expected state/events/plots, desktop driver and a reproducible result artifact.

rows.requirement: Run actual native GUI end-to-end tests
rows.acceptance: CI or dedicated test VM launches a window and drives pointer/keyboard; headless AppState selftest alone cannot satisfy GUI gate.
Baseline screenshots at 900×600, 1280×800, 1920×1080 and 100/150/200% scale reviewed for both themes.

rows.requirement: Test real cancellation with a slow kernel
rows.acceptance: GUI test cancels a script while worker is inside lengthy computation; asserts UI responsiveness, state consistency and worker termination.
Two tabs execute with different precision and variables concurrently; snapshots and plots never cross, and tab B completes while A runs.
Random edit sequences compare incremental run snapshot to fresh-run reference across dependencies, functions, effects and precision.

rows.requirement: Test editor and diagnostic UTF-16 mapping
rows.acceptance: Emoji, combining marks, CRLF, multiline, nested scopes and parse errors highlight exact location with correct accessible announcement.
Golden outputs cover exact fractions, 1k-digit numbers, matrix/inverse, solve records, MathIR, symbols, conditions and truncated prints.
Reference plot corpus rasterized in both renderers; text, strokes and clip regions compared with documented pixel tolerance and manual review.
Crash during dirty buffer edit and interrupted save are replayed; user data remains recoverable and app relaunches cleanly.

rows.requirement: Test screen reader and keyboard flows
rows.acceptance: One Windows UIA screen reader and one other supported platform accessibility path are exercised; all primary actions reachable.
At least 5 target users complete 8 scripted tasks; >=90% task success, median <2 min for common tasks, and document qualitative friction.
rows.scope_note: Human usability sessions (>=5 target users) cannot be produced by this run; waived by the user in DEC-006. Never reported as PASS.

rows.acceptance: Target System Usability Scale >=80 in pilot, with no unresolved severity-1 usability finding at launch.

rows.requirement: Audit layout/content across DPI and text scaling
rows.acceptance: Visual tests at 100/125/150/200% DPI plus system text enlargement identify no overlapping/clipped primary controls.
Theme token checker verifies normal text >=4.5:1 and large/control indicators >=3:1; exemptions documented.
Artifact manifest records OS, build SHA, Rust toolchain, source hash, GUI test results, screenshot bundle and test fixture checksums.

rows.requirement: Make unsupported features visible, not silently skipped
rows.acceptance: Feature register distinguishes PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, NOT_TESTED, APPROVED_DEVIATION; missing evidence blocks final parity.
Continuous measurements compare startup/input/frame metrics and task completion across releases, with declared regression thresholds.
